summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Acme Analytics through hosted API chat/text generation basics: streaming, common params (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), retries and idempotency, and quick Console view. Customer is evaluating hosted first for speed to delivery; main concerns were cost vs latency, retries on 5xxs, and SOC2/KMS compliance. Agreed next steps: pricing + security docs, POC scoping call.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Ok hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. we also have Priya, our solution engineer, and Sam joining.
[00:00:08] Ravi Patel (Acme): Hi Jordan, hi Priya, thanks. we've got about 40 minutes. we're mainly trying to understand how fast we can get a chat flow up and how streaming works.
[00:00:20] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Great, we'll focus on hosted API basics — chat and text generation. quick agenda: API calls, streaming demo, key params, retries and best practices, then a short Console tour. sound good?
[00:00:32] Emily Chen (Acme): yes sounds good. real quick, we have security questions too — SOC2, KMS, VPC later.
[00:00:40] Jordan: noted will cover at end and send docs. ok priya take it away.
[00:00:45] Priya: cool thanks. I'll share my screen — demo notebook, using the /v1/chat/completions style endpoint. so typical request contains messages: system user assistant, and we pass model = "redwood-medium" in hosted. note: model names in the catalog come with perf profiles.
[00:01:05] Priya: i'll do a streaming example first. we do server-sent events style streaming; payloads arrive as delta tokens and you can render them in the UI as they come. this reduces perceived latency.
[00:01:20] Mark O'Neil (Acme): does streaming use SSE or websockets?
[00:01:24] Priya: we support SSE for browsers and chunked HTTP for node/python SDKs, websocket support is on the roadmap. it's in the docs as "stream: true" param.
[00:01:35] [00:01:36] Priya: demo: request with stream=true, temperature=0.2, max_tokens=150. sending...
[00:01:45] [00:01:46] Notebook: (output) delta: "Hello"
[00:01:50] Priya: you can see tokens streaming in, and we also provide per-chunk timing metadata. sometimes the transcript from our recorder can show things like stream events as 'utterances' which is why you may see weird spacing in autogenerated transcriptions.
[00:02:10] Ravi: nice — how do you handle partial failures? mid-stream error — do we get a retry?
[00:02:18] Priya: good question. streaming retries are handled client-side typically. we recommend short-lived idempotency keys for full response retries. our SDK has helpers: if you see a transient 5xx you can retry with exponential backoff and a stable idempotency token. for streaming there is no perfect resume token right now, so best practice is either re-send with idempotency and prefer shorter outputs or checkpoint on server side in your app.
[00:02:44] Emily: so if a 502 happens at token 40, we restart and the platform will try to dedupe based on the idempotency key?
[00:02:52] Priya: yes, the idempotency key lets the hosted API dedupe identical requests within a short window. it's not like resuming the token stream — it's deduping the response generation server-side to prevent double billing.
[00:03:05] Sam Rivera (Redwood): another hook is partial caching — for many chat flows we recommend prefix caching (KV cache) for system + static context so you only regenerate dynamic parts, lowers cost.
[00:03:18] Ravi: that KV cache — is that something we have to manage?
[00:03:21] Sam: No, on hosted we do it automatically based on heuristics, or you can opt in with config. on Dedicated/Private you can control it.
[00:03:30] Priya: moving to params — temp, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences. temperature controls randomness; top_p is nucleus sampling. low temp for deterministic systems. show an example: temp=0, top_p=1 for deterministic replies; temp=0.7 for creative completions.
[00:03:50] [00:03:52] Priya: also you can set "presence_penalty" and "frequency_penalty" for chat loops. we showed these in the notebook with a small persona prompt.
[00:04:05] Emily: do you recommend going to quantized models on hosted to save cost?
[00:04:10] Priya: we expose model variants — for example redwood-medium-8bit. Optimize can recommend quantization profiles by workload; Optimize will simulate cost/loss tradeoffs for your prompt set. we can run a quick Optimize scan as part of a POC.
[00:04:26] Ravi: what's the billing model during streaming — per token generated or per request?
[00:04:30] Jordan: per-token billing still applies; streaming doesn't increase cost, it's just a transport. there may be minimums in some reserved plans but generally tokens billed are the same as non-stream.
[00:04:43] Emily: can we set max latency or SLOs on hosted?
[00:04:47] Jordan: on hosted we publish perf profiles and 99th p50 numbers; for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated. but we do routing policies to pick lower-latency variants and region routing.
[00:04:59] [00:05:00] Mark: about retries again — is there guidance for backoff params?
[00:05:04] Priya: yes sample: retry with exponential backoff starting 500ms, multiply by 2 up to 8s, jitter of 100-500ms, stop after 4 retries. for 429s also respect Retry-After header.
[00:05:20] Priya: quick demo of SDK call (node):
[00:05:22] Priya: const response = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-medium', messages, stream: true, temperature: 0.2, idempotency_key: 'acme-session-123' })
[00:05:35] Priya: note idempotency_key in SDK, and for big batches use request-level dedupe headers.
[00:05:40] Ravi: about request/response validation — can we get structured outputs?
[00:05:44] Priya: yes we support function/tool calling and structured JSON output via a schema param; the model will follow constraints; we also have a parse/validate helper in the SDK and Console shows schema run traces.
[00:05:58] Emily: demo the Console?
[00:06:00] Jordan: quick browse. (screen share) Console has routes, per-route tokens, model selection, streaming toggle, and built-in analytics. you can replay calls and inspect timing breakdowns — queue, generation, network.
[00:06:18] Jordan: here is a per-route breakdown showing tokens by system/user/assistant and cost estimation. there is a button to export prompts and you can attach test evals.
[00:06:30] Ravi: can we enable SAML SSO for teams?
[00:06:33] Jordan: yes SSO, RBAC, audit logs. we'll send the security whitepaper.
[00:06:40] [00:06:41] Priya: also quick note on retries + idempotency: for idempotency to work well include a stable serialization of messages in the key; otherwise small differences create new requests.
[00:06:55] Emily: any limits on streaming chunk size?
[00:06:58] Priya: chunks are token deltas; no hard chunk-size limit but there is a max HTTP payload size. SDKs will batch small deltas to reduce overhead.
[00:07:12] Mark: about error handling for large contexts — do you truncate or return 413?
[00:07:18] Priya: we return 400 for invalid requests, 413 for payload too large; recommend rolling window or context anchors and compress static context. we can also use embeddings to store long histories and fetch relevant context.
[00:07:32] Ravi: can you demonstrate a retry scenario?
[00:07:35] Priya: i can simulate a 502 in the notebook — re-sending with same idempotency key.
[00:07:44] [00:07:46] Notebook: (simulated) initial stream aborted at 00:08:12 with 502
[00:07:50] Priya: now resend with same idempotency_key, you should see the same or deduped result and only one billing event recorded.
[00:08:00] Emily: good. what about request timeouts?
[00:08:04] Priya: client-side timeouts recommended at 60s default for chat, but depends; you can also set server-side per-route timeouts on Dedicated. hosted will cut long running jobs after a threshold (we'll include exact numbers in docs).
[00:08:18] Jordan: quick question from our side — what is your target for go-live for this chat beta?
[00:08:22] Ravi: ideally end of Q2; we need a small POC by mid-March to validate latency and cost.
[00:08:28] Jordan: perfect, we'll propose a POC scope after this.
[00:08:34] Priya: a few additional best practices: 1) use batching for high throughput, 2) prefix cache for static context, 3) instrument tokens and latencies for regressions, 4) use Optimize to get quantization suggestions.
[00:08:50] Ravi: can Optimize run against our prompt set?
[00:08:53] Priya: yes, you upload prompts/evals via Console or API, Optimize will recommend batches, quantization, and model variants — gives estimated cost delta and expected quality loss. we can include an Optimize trial in the POC.
[00:09:06] Emily: security — we need KMS integration and audit logs retained 12 months. is that supported on hosted?
[00:09:14] Jordan: hosted supports TLS in transit and encryption at rest; customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated/Private. for hosted we have managed KMS; for enterprise customers we do KMS integrations. audit logs available as add-on retention. we'll include this in follow-up.
[00:09:30] Mark: about regional compliance — can we pin region?
[00:09:33] Jordan: yes you can pick region in hosted if we have the region; for strict data residency Dedicated/Private is recommended.
[00:09:40] [00:09:42] Priya: returning to examples — i'll show setting stop sequences to avoid run-on replies. set stop: ["

", "###"] for chat completions.
[00:09:55] Priya: also deterministic sampling (temp=0) combined with stop works well for structured data.
[00:10:05] Ravi: any gotchas with streaming and proxies in our infra? we use corp proxies and sometimes chunked responses are buffered.
[00:10:12] Priya: yep proxy buffering is a common issue; we recommend long-lived SSE or websockets when possible and testing via your corp proxy. the Console has a debug mode to capture round trips.
[00:10:26] Emily: how do we estimate cost for a given flow?
[00:10:29] Jordan: use tokens per prompt estimate x expected requests per month; Console's per-route cost estimator shows historical estimates. Optimize can report cost delta for model swaps.
[00:10:40] Priya: also provide sample backoff code in the demo notebook.
[00:10:45] [00:10:46] Priya: small aside on naming — sometimes our docs refer to Redwood Optimize as "Optimize" or "Redwood Optimize" and earlier internal docs had typo "RedWood Opt" — ignore that, it's the same product.
[00:10:58] Ravi: ha ok. one last technical: how do you surface partial tokens in streaming — do you get low-level token ids?
[00:11:04] Priya: streaming gives text deltas and optional token metadata if you enable streaming_tokens flag. token ids are not always exposed in hosted for some models, but we can provide log-level traces in Console for debugging.
[00:11:20] Mark: ok we're getting to time — quick recap and next steps please.
[00:11:25] Jordan: recap: 1) Hosted API supports streaming (SSE/chunked), dedupe via idempotency_key, retry guidance with exponential backoff, prefix/KV caching to save cost, Optimize for quantization suggestions, and Console for per-route analytics. 2) Security: send SOC2/KMS docs and audit log options. 3) POC: scope to test latency and cost; target mid-March.
[00:11:50] Jordan: next steps we've captured: send pricing + security pack, propose POC scope, schedule POC scoping call.
[00:11:58] Ravi: thanks everyone — we'll look for the emails.
[00:12:02] Emily: thanks, appreciate the demo.
[00:12:05] Jordan: thanks all, end call.
[00:12:10] [END OF TRANSCRIPT NOTE] The transcript has been edited for readability but retains ASR artifacts and occasional mislabels (e.g., some speakers show generic 'Unidentified Speaker').
